# 1c Cloudflare, embedded xray, endpoints: contract

**Read first:** [Cloudflare](../integrations/cloudflare.md), [VLESS XHTTP](../integrations/vless-xhttp.md) (connection URI, checks), [ADR 0009](../adr/0009-embedded-xray-core-no-docker-socket.md), [servers module → Endpoints, DNS](../modules/servers.md#endpoints-and-connection-uris), [health → Checks](../processes/servers/server-health.md#checks) (the proxy test only), [open questions](../open-questions.md) "To verify" 6, the 1a and 1b **As built**.

**Done when:** xray-core is embedded; a `vless-xhttp-tls` endpoint builds the exact connection URI and runs the proxy test against an in-process VLESS XHTTP server with classified failures; the `xray` validator rejects configs xray refuses; the Cloudflare driver creates, finds, updates and deletes Proxier's A records and waits for them on two resolvers; Settings → Integrations → Cloudflare and Settings → Servers exist; the IP → country lookup works; open question 6's binary-size half is answered; every checklist line has its test.

Nothing here touches a server yet. Provisioning (1d) composes these parts.

## Decisions

| Topic | Decision | Why |
|---|---|---|
| xray as a library | `github.com/xtls/xray-core` at the latest release tag; import `_ "github.com/xtls/xray-core/main/distro/all"` **only** in `servers/proxy` (keeps it out of every other package's tests). Configs are built as xray JSON (the same shape a client app uses) and loaded with `infra/conf/serial.LoadJSONConfig` → `core.New`. One instance per proxy test, closed after it. | ADR 0009. JSON is xray's stable surface; protobuf internals move between releases. |
| xray logging and instances | Every config Proxier builds sets `"log": {"loglevel": "none", "access": "none"}`: a started instance installs xray's **global** log handler, which writes to stdout in its own format and would break the JSON logs. Up to 8 instances run at once (the `checks` queue); each is its own `core.Instance`, started and closed by the proxy test. `ValidateConfig` never starts one, so a template's own `log` section doesn't matter there. | xray's log handler is process-wide. |
| Client config | One outbound `vless` with `users: [{id, encryption: "none"}]`, `streamSettings: {network: "xhttp", security: "tls", tlsSettings: {serverName: sni, fingerprint: fp, alpn: [alpn]}, xhttpSettings: {path, mode, host}}`; no inbounds. Connections through it with `core.Dial(ctx, instance, xnet.TCPDestination(…))`. | The proxy test must connect "exactly as a real client does". |
| Proxy test | `proxy.Test(ctx, ep, Options)`: (1) direct TCP connect to `host:port`, 5 s → `tcp-timeout` / `tcp-refused`; (2) direct TLS handshake with the endpoint's SNI and ALPN, 5 s → `tls-failed`; (3) HTTP GET of the test URL through the xray dialer (`http.Transport.DialContext` = xray), overall timeout (15 s), a stall timer reset on every read (5 s) → `stalled` with the bytes received, a non-2xx → `http-error`, the overall deadline → `timeout`. Success records connect ms (step 1), TLS ms (step 2), time to first byte and throughput (bytes / transfer time) and the bytes received. Steps 1–2 classify; step 3 decides. | health.md's classes. xray's errors are opaque; the direct probes make the class deterministic. |
| Test URL | Template `proxy_test.url` if set, else `servers.proxy_test_url`. The URL used is in the result. A result whose body is under 64 KiB carries `warning: "small-object"` (the UI shows "test object is N KB; throttling after ~20 KB can't be seen"). | health.md. |
| Test options | `Options{Timeout, Stall, Insecure bool, Resolve map[string]string}`; `Insecure` and `Resolve` exist for tests (self-signed certificate, `host → 127.0.0.1:port`) and are never set from settings. | |
| `proxytest` | `proxy/proxytest.Server`: an in-process xray **server** instance (VLESS inbound, `network: xhttp`, `security: tls` with a generated self-signed certificate, `freedom` outbound) on 127.0.0.1, plus an `httptest` test-object server with modes `OK(n bytes)`, `StallAfter(n)`, `Status(code)`, `Slow(firstByte)`; and `CloseTCP()` / `RejectTLS()` switches to produce the direct-probe failures. | No network in tests. |
| Config validation | `proxy.ValidateConfig(json []byte) error`: `serial.LoadJSONConfig` + `core.New` (not started) + `Close`. Wired into `validate.XrayConfig` in `Init`. | template-authoring.md `xray` row. |
| Dialer | `proxy.Dialer(ctx, ep, opts) (DialFunc, io.Closer, error)` keeps one xray instance open for the caller (discovery in Phase 3 uses it through the `ProxyDialer` port). | modules/servers.md ports. |
| Endpoint types | Registry in `servers/endpoint`: `Type{Name, Check(RenderedEndpoint) []string, URI(Endpoint) string (the display name is a field of Endpoint), ProxyConfig(Endpoint) ([]byte, error)}`. Only `vless-xhttp-tls`. Its `Check`: credential is a UUID, `path` starts with `/` and is URL-safe, `sni` non-empty, `mode` in `auto packet-up stream-up stream-one`, `fp` in xray's fingerprint list, `alpn` non-empty. Wired into `validate.EndpointFields`. | 1a left the hook. |
| URI | Exactly [vless-xhttp.md#connection-uri](../integrations/vless-xhttp.md#connection-uri): parameter order `encryption, security, sni, fp, host, alpn, type, path, mode`; `path` = `%2F` + the rest unchanged (hex); fragment percent-encoded UTF-8 (`url.PathEscape` semantics, spaces as `%20`). A golden test pins the seed's URI byte for byte. | Apps compare them. |
| Display name | `{flag} {location name} {number}`, plus ` · {key}` when the server has more than one endpoint. Location name as the admin entered it (one language) in Phase 1; per-language names wait for Phase 2's link language. | servers.md; noted in Doc changes. |
| Cloudflare client | Own client (`net/http`, JSON, base URL configurable), bearer token, 15 s per request. Methods: `VerifyToken`, `Zones`, `FindA(zoneID, name)`, `CreateA`, `UpdateA`, `DeleteRecord`. `429` → wait `Retry-After` (≤ 60 s, else 10 s) and retry inside the call, up to 5 times; `5xx` and network errors → 3 retries with 1 s, 3 s, 9 s; `401`/`403` → `ErrTokenRejected` (permanent, message names the zone); others → error with Cloudflare's message. The token never appears in errors. | cloudflare.md. |
| Records | Type `A`, `proxied: false`, `ttl: 60`, `comment: "proxier:<server name>"`. | |
| Ensure | `Driver.Ensure(ctx, name, ip, serverName, overwrite)`: zone = longest allowed suffix; find existing A at the name. None → create. One with Proxier's comment for **this** server → update content if different (a retry). Anything else → `*ConflictError{Name, Content, Comment}` unless `overwrite`, which updates it in place and sets Proxier's comment. Returns the record (with id) for `servers_dns_records`. | Never touch records Proxier didn't create, unless told. |
| Wait | `Waiter.Wait(ctx, name, ip, log)`: every 10 s ask Cloudflare and Google **over DNS-over-HTTPS** (RFC 8484 GET, `application/dns-message`, built with `golang.org/x/net/dns/dnsmessage`) at IP-addressed URLs `https://1.1.1.1/dns-query` and `https://8.8.8.8/dns-query`, until both answer with the IP, or 10 min → `ErrNotVisible` naming which resolver answered what. A resolver whose DoH request fails at the network level is asked over plain UDP `1.1.1.1:53` / `8.8.8.8:53` instead (`net.Resolver{PreferGo: true, Dial}`), and the log says which transport answered. Selects on cancellation. Resolvers, transports and the interval are fields (tests: a fake `Lookup`). | Proxier sits behind the home MikroTik, which may intercept port 53; DoH reaches the real resolvers. |
| Delete | `Driver.Remove(ctx, rec, serverName, ip)`: fetch by id; delete only if the content is still the IP **and** the comment is still Proxier's for that server; otherwise return `Kept{reason}`. A 404 counts as removed. | retirement.md. |
| Settings → Cloudflare | Page `/settings/integrations/cloudflare` (a row on Integrations): token field (secret); on save, `VerifyToken` + `Zones` first and nothing saved on refusal ("Cloudflare refused this token"); then the zone list with checkboxes (`cloudflare.zones`, names, comma-separated), **Test** re-lists zones. The hostname pattern's zone must be among the ticked ones: the Servers settings page shows a warning when it isn't. | cloudflare.md setup. |
| IP → country | `geoip.Lookup(ctx, pattern, ip)`: `pattern` is `servers.ip_country_url` with `{ip}`; GET with 3 s timeout; body trimmed, must be two letters → upper case; anything else → `""`. Empty pattern → no request. The admin's IP never leaves; only the server's IP. | User decision 2026-10-07. |
| Settings → Servers | Page `/settings/servers` (a `SettingsPage`, order 35) with the `servers` section: hostname pattern, IP country URL, proxy test URL, timeout, stall. Health fields join it in 1f. | |

Settings, added to section `servers` and a new section `cloudflare`:

| Key | Kind | Default | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|
| `servers.ip_country_url` | string | `https://ipinfo.io/{ip}/country` | empty = off; must contain `{ip}` and be https |
| `servers.proxy_test_url` | string | `https://speed.cloudflare.com/__down?bytes=262144` | http(s) |
| `servers.proxy_test_timeout` | duration | `15s` | 5 s – 2 min |
| `servers.proxy_test_stall` | duration | `5s` | 1 s – 60 s |
| `cloudflare.api_token` | secret | `""` | |
| `cloudflare.zones` | string | `""` | allowed zone names, comma-separated |

## Go signatures

### `servers/endpoint`

```go
type Endpoint struct {
	Key, Type, Host, Credential string
	Port                        int
	Params                      map[string]string
	DisplayName                 string
}
type Type struct {
	Name        string
	Check       func(e render.RenderedEndpoint) []string
	URI         func(e Endpoint) string
	ProxyConfig func(e Endpoint) ([]byte, error) // xray client JSON
}
func Lookup(name string) (Type, bool)
func DisplayName(flag, locationName string, number int, key string, many bool) string
```

### `servers/proxy`

```go
type Class string // "" (ok) tcp-timeout tcp-refused tls-failed stalled http-error timeout
type Options struct {
	URL            string
	Timeout, Stall time.Duration
	Insecure       bool              // tests only
	Resolve        map[string]string // tests only: "host:port" → "127.0.0.1:port"
}
type Result struct {
	OK          bool
	Class       Class
	Error       string
	URL         string
	ConnectMS, TLSMS, FirstByteMS int
	Bytes       int64
	ThroughputKbps int
	SmallObject bool
}
func Test(ctx context.Context, e endpoint.Endpoint, o Options) Result
type DialFunc func(ctx context.Context, network, addr string) (net.Conn, error)
func Dialer(ctx context.Context, e endpoint.Endpoint, o Options) (DialFunc, io.Closer, error)
func ValidateConfig(config []byte) error
```

### `servers/dns`

```go
type Record struct {
	Provider, ZoneID, Zone, Name, Type, Content, RecordID string
}
type ConflictError struct{ Name, Content, Comment string }
var ErrNotVisible = errors.New("dns: the record is not visible on every resolver yet")
type Kept struct{ Reason string } // "points to 198.51.100.7", "comment changed"

type Driver interface {
	Ensure(ctx context.Context, name, ip, serverName string, overwrite bool) (Record, error)
	Remove(ctx context.Context, r Record, serverName, ip string) (removed bool, kept Kept, err error)
	Covers(ctx context.Context, name string) (zone string, ok bool, err error) // the form's check
}
type Resolver struct {
	Name string // "Cloudflare", "Google"
	DoH  string // "https://1.1.1.1/dns-query"
	UDP  string // "1.1.1.1:53": the fallback
}
type Waiter struct {
	Resolvers []Resolver
	Every     time.Duration
	Timeout   time.Duration
	HTTP      *http.Client
	// Lookup replaces both transports in tests; transport is "doh" or "udp".
	Lookup func(ctx context.Context, r Resolver, name string) (addrs []netip.Addr, transport string, err error)
}
func (w Waiter) Wait(ctx context.Context, name, ip string, log *jobs.Logger) error
```

### `servers/dns/cloudflare`

```go
var ErrTokenRejected = errors.New("cloudflare: token rejected or lacks DNS edit")
type Client struct{ BaseURL string; HTTP *http.Client; Sleep func(time.Duration) }
func New(token string) *Client
func (c *Client) VerifyToken(ctx context.Context) error
func (c *Client) Zones(ctx context.Context) ([]Zone, error)
// Driver is settings-backed: it reads the token and the allowed zones on each call.
func NewDriver(st *settings.Store, newClient func(token string) *Client) dns.Driver
```

## As built

Done 2026-10-07. Every checklist line has its test, in the file the line names. `make check`'s parts (templ, gofmt, vet, `make test`), `make lint` (0 issues) and `docker build .` are green; the image starts, migrates, seeds the template and answers `/healthz`. Deviations and notes for 1d and later:

- **The spike (open question 6, first half).** xray-core `v1.260327.0` embeds with `CGO_ENABLED=0`. Stripped binary (as the Dockerfile builds it): **47.3 → 62.4 MB**; image **71 → 92.8 MB** (the binary inside it is 62.8 MB); unstripped host binary 67.4 → 88.8 MB. The first build after adding it took 17 s on the host with xray compiled from scratch and everything else cached. No cgo, no new system libraries. The second half (XHTTP `stream-up` through the real nginx `grpc_pass`) is 1d's, on a real VPS: `proxytest` is an xray server and accepts any mode, so nothing here says anything about nginx. `docs/open-questions.md` 6 says so.
- **`make test` runs the xray packages without `-race`.** xray's own XHTTP client has a data race (`splithttp.WaitReadCloser.Set` writes `ReadCloser` while `Read` checks it; reported by the first proxy test through `proxytest`). Not ours to fix, so the Makefile's `test` is `go test -race` for every package except `./internal/modules/servers/proxy/...`, which run plain (`XRAY_TESTS` in the Makefile), and CI now runs `make test` instead of its own line. **Any later test that pushes XHTTP traffic (1d's harness with `proxytest`, 1f) must either live in those packages or the Makefile's list grows.** Tests that only call `proxy.ValidateConfig` (the `servers` package, `validate`) are fine under `-race`.
- **`proxy.Options` differs from the contract.** `Insecure bool` is gone: this xray no longer has `allowInsecure` (building a config with it is an error after 2026-06-01), so a self-signed test server is trusted by pinning: `PinCert` is the SHA-256 (hex) of the one certificate to accept, written as `pinnedPeerCertSha256` into the client config and used by the direct TLS probe too. Added: `Probe` (each direct probe, default 5 s) and `Dial` (replaces the direct TCP probe's dialer, so a blackhole is simulated without waiting on the network). `Resolve` also changes the address and port of the xray outbound, while the SNI and the HTTP host stay the endpoint's. All three are for tests and never come from settings. `Class` constants are `proxy.OK`, `TCPTimeout`, `TCPRefused`, `TLSFailed`, `Stalled`, `HTTPError`, `Timeout`.
- **How `proxy.Test` classifies, beyond the contract.** A failing probe returns at once. Dial errors that are neither a timeout nor a refusal (no route, DNS failure) are `tcp-timeout` with the real text in `Error`. The TLS probe uses **uTLS with the endpoint's fingerprint** (xray's own table, `tls.GetFingerprint`) and verifies the certificate itself (system roots, the SNI; or the pin), so a network that treats a Go ClientHello differently from Chrome's does not mislead it; an expired certificate is therefore `tls-failed`, not a late `http-error`. Step 3: the stall timer is armed when step 3 starts and restarts on every read from the xray connection, so a tunnel that never delivers a byte is `stalled` with 0 bytes; the overall deadline is `timeout`; a request that fails any other way (a rotated credential gives `EOF`) is `http-error`. A cancelled context returns `Class: timeout, Error: "cancelled"`. Timings are at least 1 ms when measured. `ThroughputKbps` is body bytes over the time from the first byte.
- **`proxy.ValidateConfig`** replaces the template's own `log` section before loading: building an instance registers a process-wide log handler, and a template's `loglevel: warning` would make xray print to stdout. A JSON syntax error is reported with xray's reader (line and character); xray's error chain keeps its ` > ` separators with the `infra/conf:` prefixes dropped, e.g. `failed to build inbound config with tag  > failed to load inbound detour config for protocol nope > unknown config id: nope`. It never starts the instance.
- **`TestConcurrentProxyTestsStayQuiet` has a control.** xray logs through a goroutine, so output arrives late; the test waits 300 ms before it looks and first starts a deliberately loud instance to prove it can hear xray at all (it fails if that is silent).
- **`endpoint`.** `Type.ProxyConfig` is `func(Endpoint, ProxyOptions) ([]byte, error)` (`ProxyOptions{Address, Port, PinCert}`), `Check` is also `endpoint.Check(RenderedEndpoint)` (what `validate.EndpointFields` is set to), plus `Names()`. The field check also refuses a UUID that is not in canonical form (braces and `urn:` are valid for `uuid.Parse` but not for apps) and a path with anything but letters, digits and `. _ ~ - /`. The URI's `host=` is `params.host` when the template sets one, else the endpoint host; `alpn` and the others go through `url.QueryEscape` (so `h2,http/1.1` becomes `h2%2Chttp%2F1.1`). No `#fragment` when the display name is empty.
- **`proxytest.Server`.** `New(t)`; `Endpoint()`, `Resolve()`, `ObjectURL()`, `SetMode(Mode)` with `OK(n)`, `StallAfter(n)`, `Status(code)`, `Slow(firstByte, n)`; `CloseTCP()`, `RejectTLS()` (a plain listener on the same port that hangs up), and **`Rotate(uuid, path)`** (restarts the xray server with other values; the zero value keeps the current one; 1d's harness uses it to give the server the template's generated values). `Server.UUID`, `Path`, `Port`, `CertSHA256` are exported. Its self-signed certificate is for `proxy.test`; its xray server logs nothing.
- **`dns`.** Waits take `dns.Log` (`Info`, `Warn`; `*jobs.Logger` satisfies it) instead of `*jobs.Logger`, so tests need no job. `Waiter` is built with `dns.NewWaiter()` (the two default resolvers, 10 s, 10 min, an 8 s HTTP client); `dns.DefaultResolvers`. A DoH answer that is NXDOMAIN counts as an answer ("nothing"); an HTTP error status or an unreadable answer falls back to UDP like a network failure. The log gets a line when a resolver's answer or transport changes, not every round. Also in `dns`: `ErrNotCovered`, `ErrNotConfigured`, `Comment(serverName)`, `ZoneFor`, `SplitZones`.
- **`cloudflare`.** `Client.Sleep` takes a context (`func(ctx, d) error`) so a cancel ends a retry wait. `Client` also has `GetA`, `ErrNotFound`; `UpdateA` is a PUT of the whole record (so a proxied or re-TTL'd record of ours comes back to DNS-only, 60 s). The driver chooses the zone from the setting, then needs the zone id from `Zones` (one call per `Ensure`/`Remove` of a name; no cache). A rejected token comes back as `jobs.Permanent(fmt.Errorf("%w on <zone>", ErrTokenRejected))`; a token Cloudflare accepts but whose zone list lacks the allowed zone is permanent too. `Ensure` with `overwrite` and several records at the name updates the first and deletes the others. `Remove` with a missing token returns `dns.ErrNotConfigured`. The package also declares `cloudflare.Section` (`cloudflare.api_token` secret, `cloudflare.zones`) and the key constants. `cloudflaretest.Fake` is an HTTP server speaking the API (verify, zones with paging, record CRUD) with `Fail(route, statuses…)`, `RateLimit`, `RejectToken`, `AddRecord`, `Change`, `Drop`, `Count`, `Calls`, `EchoAuth`; `Fake.Client()` / `ClientFor(token)` return a client whose retries do not sleep (`Slept()` lists what it would have), and `Fake.Driver(t, allowedZones…)` a settings-backed driver on a real store.
- **Settings.** New package `servers/conf` holds the `servers` section and its keys (the pages need them and cannot import `servers`); `servers.Section` and `servers.HostnamePatternKey` re-export. New fields as contracted: `ip_country_url` (empty or https with `{ip}`), `proxy_test_url` (http/https), `proxy_test_timeout` 5 s – 2 min, `proxy_test_stall` 1 s – 1 min; messages for labels and help in EN/RU. Validation messages of a field are English (they come from the settings store, as everywhere).
- **Platform changes.** (1) `module.IntegrationDeclarer` (`Integrations(ctx) []ui.IntegrationRow`) adds rows to Settings → Integrations after Telegram and Tailnet; `ui.IntegrationRow` replaces the pages' private row type. (2) `web.Routes.SettingsPages func() []ui.SettingsPage` gives a module's own settings page the side menu (`ui.SettingsLayout`). (3) `app.css` has `.field label.check` for the zone checkboxes (accent colour rose). (4) `ci.yaml` and the Makefile as above.
- **Pages** (`servers/pages`): `GET/POST /settings/servers` (the generic `ui.SettingsForm`, the zone warning above it with a link to the Cloudflare page; the warning also shows when no zone is allowed at all) and the four Cloudflare routes. The token form says "Check and save"; a refused token answers 422, an unreachable Cloudflare 502, and neither saves anything nor echoes the token. The zone list is fetched from Cloudflare on every page load (so the page needs the token to work; a failing list shows its reason beside the allowed zones), and saving ticks keeps only zones the token sees. `Module.CloudflareClient` is the seam tests use. The Integrations row reads "Token saved · allowed zones: N". **Not exercised in a real browser.**
- **Module wiring.** `Init` sets `validate.XrayConfig = proxy.ValidateConfig` and `validate.EndpointFields = endpoint.Check` (package globals, idempotent), builds `Module.DNS` (settings-backed Cloudflare driver; reads `Module.CloudflareClient` at call time) and `Module.Waiter`. `TestModuleWiresValidators` pins it. Importing `proxy` into `servers` links xray into every test binary that includes the module (`sitetest` users); none of them starts XHTTP, so they stay under `-race`.
- **Display name** has no caller yet: 1d computes `endpoint.DisplayName(country.Flag, location.Name, number, key, many)` when it writes endpoints.
- **Notes for 1d.** The smoke test calls `proxy.Test` with `Options{URL, Timeout, Stall}` from `servers.proxy_test_*` (or the template's `proxy_test.url`) and, in the harness, `Resolve` + `PinCert` from `proxytest`. `proxy.Dialer` takes the same options. `geoip.Lookup(ctx, pattern, ip)` reads `servers.ip_country_url`; `geoip.Client` is a package variable for tests. `dns.Driver.Covers` is the form's check and needs no Cloudflare call. A `*dns.ConflictError` should be made permanent by the provision job (the driver returns it plain); `jobs.IsPermanent` already holds for a rejected token. Not built: a proxy test of a stored endpoint (1f) or any caller of these parts outside tests.
